name: Holland Village
blurb: The classic first-landing expat neighbourhood: cafes, bars, a wet market, and an MRT on the Circle Line. Walkable, social, and priced like it.
vibe: Leafy high-street, weekend crowds, old-school expat hangout that still works.
watch: Weekend noise on the strip. Demand stays firm; negotiate on 2-year leases.

name: Tanjong Pagar
blurb: Finance and tech workers live on top of the office. Korean and Japanese food, Duxton shophouses, and a five-minute walk to Tanjong Pagar MRT.
vibe: Urban, loud at lunch, quiet-ish at night once the suits leave.
watch: Smaller units. Parking is painful. Great if you never want a car.

name: River Valley / Orchard
blurb: Prime, central, and unapologetically expensive. Orchard shopping, Robertson Quay drinks, and condos that sell the skyline.
vibe: Polished, tourist-adjacent, every amenity stacked on top of itself.
watch: You pay for the postcode. Families often get more space in D10 or D15 for the same money.

name: Tiong Bahru
blurb: Art-deco low-rise, independent cafes, a legendary wet market, and two MRT lines. The neighbourhood that made 'old Singapore' fashionable.
vibe: Village-in-the-city. Brunch queues, heritage blocks, slightly smug — earned.
watch: Limited new condo stock. HDB rentals here are competitive; check eligibility.

name: East Coast / Katong
blurb: Sea breeze, Peranakan shophouses, longer units for the money, and the Thomson-East Coast Line making this a genuine CBD alternative.
vibe: Laid-back east. Joo Chiat nights, East Coast Park mornings, chilli crab.
watch: TEL has changed the calculus. Rents have firmed since the line opened.

name: Bukit Timah
blurb: Green, hilly, and built around schools. Landed houses, older condos, the Rail Corridor, and a quieter life than Holland V.
vibe: Residential, greenery, weekend cycling. Not a nightlife district.
watch: You live here for schools and space, not F&B. Car is useful but not mandatory.

name: Woodlands
blurb: The American-school belt. Larger condos, Causeway convenience, and a real trade-off: you are in the far north.
vibe: Suburban, mall-centric, family. Weekend trips across the Causeway.
watch: Great if the school is SAS. Painful if your office is in the CBD five days a week.

name: Serangoon / Kovan
blurb: Australian and French school catchment, NEL access, heartland malls, and more square footage than the centre.
vibe: Residential heartland with a strong school-run rhythm.
watch: Check school bus routes before you sign. A 2km difference matters at 7am.

name: Newton / Novena
blurb: Hospitals, good food, and a straight shot down the North-South Line. Underrated for professionals who want central without Orchard prices.
vibe: Grown-up central. Newton hawker, medical hub, older condos with size.
watch: Novena is a medical cluster — traffic around Mount E and TTSH is real.

name: HarbourFront / Sentosa
blurb: Water, malls, and the island. Sentosa condos are a lifestyle purchase; HarbourFront is more practical with the Circle and North-East lines.
vibe: Weekend-every-day on Sentosa; transit hub at HarbourFront.
watch: Sentosa has extra costs (island fees, fewer buses). Test the commute at rush hour.

name: Clementi / West Coast
blurb: NUS, one-north, science parks, and a west-side value play. Strong MRT, hawker centres that locals actually use, and Dover/Clementi school buses.
vibe: Academic-west. Practical, less polished, better food than the marketing suggests.
watch: one-north workers should look at Buona Vista / one-north condos first.

name: Punggol / Sengkang
blurb: New waterfront towns, North-East Line, and some of the best new-condo value on the island. Young families, not the classic expat trail.
vibe: Planned new town. Waterway, playgrounds, malls, longish CBD ride.
watch: International school buses are longer. Great if you do not need a D10 postcode.

name: Yishun
blurb: The north that is not Woodlands. North-South Line, Northpoint, a real hospital, Lower Seletar at dawn. Internet jokes aside, this is how a lot of Singapore actually lives — and rents like it.
vibe: Town centre + reservoir. Peak-hour trains, Chong Pang evenings, no Holland Village strip.
schools: SAS / Tanglin are a long bus (Woodlands or Bukit Timah instead)
watch: Do not rent here for an international-school run. Do rent here if you want space, KTPH nearby, and a 1-bed that is not D9 money. NSL is packed 8am. Canberra is quieter than Yishun Central.

name: Kampong Glam / Bugis
blurb: Sultan, Haji Lane, Arab Street, and Bugis as a real commute. Walkable, loud on Friday night, grocery on North Bridge. You live next to the postcard, which is the feature and the complaint.
bestFor: People who want the city without D9 rent
vibe: Heritage streets, weekend crowds, weekday kopi. Not a school-bus neighbourhood.
schools: Limited international options nearby — bus or live west/east instead
watch: Friday–Saturday noise on Haji Lane is not a rumour. Conservation walk-ups mean stairs and thin walls. Great if you walk everywhere; misery if you need a parking lot and a Tanglin bus.

name: Little India / Farrer Park
blurb: Tekka, Mustafa at 2am, Race Course Road, and a real NEL commute. Deepavali is the loud month. The rest of the year this is groceries, gold shops, and more space than Kampong Glam for the money.
vibe: Market streets, 24-hour fluorescent, Farrer Park condos above the fray. Weekend temple crowds.
schools: Not an international-school belt — bus out or live north/west
eat: Mustafa (when you need a frying pan at 1am)
watch: Deepavali lights go up weeks before 8 November — beautiful and packed. Street noise and incense are the deal. Farrer Park / City Square is the condo version of the same postcode. Serangoon Gardens is a different north-east entirely.
